title: Security: secrets and env isolation
description: Env vars and secrets live only in the kernel/shell-interaction layer. Model-bound content carries symbolic refs (e.g. {{env/API_KEY}}) resolved at process-spawn time; values never enter context assembly, the journal, or the events stream (journal content is model-visible on resume, so redact before write). Redaction filter over tool output for known secret values as a backstop. Base on dirge's handling - design notes to follow from the dirge security survey.
design:
Dirge basis (paths under /Users/yogthos/src/dirge-code/dirge/src):
- Env stripping before EVERY spawn: scrub_env at sandbox/mod.rs:766, called unconditionally from build_command :443. Name-based strip (KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD + explicit cloud-cred list, is_sensitive_env_name :614) with SAFE_EXACT re-permits (SSH_AUTH_SOCK, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN :640); value-shape detection (sk-, AKIA, ghp_, hf_, xox*, URL userinfo; is_sensitive_env_value :674) replaces with [REDACTED]; known stripped values also matched by substring so aliased vars are caught.
- Single redaction boundary: content_value_to_block at agent/agent_loop/tools.rs:915-932 runs redact_secrets (impl sandbox/mod.rs:849) on every tool-result block before it reaches LLM context, persisted transcript, or UI. Threat model named in the comment: cat .env / echo $API_KEY.
- Ingestion guard on stored knowledge: extras/content_guard.rs scans memory/skill writes and tool-result ingestion for injection, invisible-Unicode smuggling, exfil patterns; memory re-scanned at prompt-render time.
- API key storage: auth/store.rs + auth/file_store.rs - atomic write, chmod 0600 file / 0700 dir, permissions tightened on save.
Dirge caveat we go beyond: its redaction is pattern-based, so an opaque secret with no vendor prefix can leak. Karamazov inverts the default - symbolic refs ({{env/NAME}}) resolved only at process-spawn in the kernel, so values never enter model space at all; dirge-style boundary redaction remains as the backstop layer.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: plant a canary secret, run a live task that uses it by reference; assert the canary value appears in no model-bound payload, journal row, or event.

title: Security: shell command permission system
description: Dirge-based: allowlist matching, session vs global layering, approval flow for non-allowlisted commands, persistence in the db. Enforced at the tool-dispatch cell so it governs every effectful shell path, not just one tool. Design notes to follow from the dirge security survey.
design:
Dirge basis (paths under /Users/yogthos/src/dirge-code/dirge/src):
- Two-stage policy engine: Engine::authorize at permission/engine/mod.rs:123. Stage A deciders in fixed precedence, first-claim-wins (order is the vec at engine/build.rs:196-224: ReservedDeviceName -> PromptDeny -> Yolo -> ConfiguredDeny -> SessionAllowlist -> ConfiguredRule -> BuiltinAllow -> ExternalDir -> DefaultAction); stage B modifiers may only tighten (fold = Effect::meet, order-independent). Multiple resources fold most-restrictive-wins -> one decision, at most one prompt.
- Rules are (op, tool, pattern, effect), ordered, LAST match wins (permission/mod.rs:103-114); glob style inferred from op. Head-anchored deny candidates so 'FOO=1 rm -rf /' / 'nohup rm -rf /' still hit denies (engine/build.rs:480-503); strip_module_runner for 'python -m tool' (permission/mod.rs:184-223); $(...) compounds become a whole-command 'complex' resource so 'echo $(rm -rf ~)' cannot ride an 'echo **' allow (engine/types.rs:98, engine/policies.rs:245-290).
- Curated base rules, not heuristics: base_bash_rules at permission/mod.rs:225-420 - read-only / project-dev / fs-mutator buckets, hard denies (rm -rf /**, dd, mkfs...), and a deliberate always-prompt list (npx, node, git push, git rebase/reset, npm/pip install, sudo, curl/wget).
- Approval flow: enforce chokepoints at agent/tools/mod.rs:879+. On Ask: optional LLM judge (permission/approval.rs - fails closed, ALLOW must be a bare line, evaluator Deny escalates to human rather than short-circuiting) then human ask over channel (permission/ask.rs); deny-with-note folds the note into the tool-result error so the model gets redirection; headless auto-denies.
- Persistence/layering: session allowlist on Session (session/mod.rs:324), installed live on allow-always, restored at startup, cleared on cwd change so no privilege carry-over (permission/checker.rs:493-502); global ~/.config/dirge/config.json merged key-by-key with project .dirge/config.json, user rules appended after builtins so last-match-wins favors them; SecurityMode precedence Yolo > Accept > Restrictive > Standard, Accept loosens only low-risk in-tree ops.
For karamazov: rules-as-EDN fits naturally; the decider chain becomes pure functions/cells so the policy itself is inspectable data in the state machine; session grants persist in the db; enforcement lives in the tool-dispatch cell.
acceptance_criteria: Live run: allowlisted command runs; non-allowlisted command blocks and surfaces an approval; a grant persists for the session and is visible in the db.

title: Agentic loop as a mycelium manifest - first live milestone
description: Express the minimal loop as a workflow manifest stored in the db and loaded at boot: context assembly -> inference (DeepSeek adapter + fence parse) -> tool dispatch -> journal append -> arbiter gate (at most one steer per turn boundary, the veriframe/dirge-validated pattern) -> route. Cells come from the pruned veriframe core. Work is grounded in a task from the tasks board. This is the milestone every later task hangs off.
design:
Mycelium application map (from docs survey; sources in mycelium-clj.github.io/resources/md/, quick-reference.md is the superset):
- The loop row IS a manifest: EDN with :id :doc :cells :edges :dispatches :interceptors :regions (+ :resilience :transforms). :doc required per cell; :on-error mandatory in strict mode (nil = considered, none needed). :schema :inherit pulls from the registry so the db row stores routing, not duplicated Malli.
- Cell naming is load-bearing: name cells :llm/*, :tool/*, :journal/*, :gate/*, :loop/* so glob-scoped interceptors give journaling ({:scope :all}) and permission-marking ({:id-match "tool/*"}) on every future agent-authored cell for free. Interceptors are pure data->data: they can MARK a denial, never enforce it - the refusal is a dispatch on the key they set.
- Validate-step chain (the mutation protocol's static half, all existing): validate-manifest -> manifest->workflow -> pre-compile (throws on ~11 structural checks) -> dev/analyze-workflow -> dev/enumerate-paths (assert ship path + loop path) -> dev/workflow-status (refuse :pending cells) -> sys/schema-conflicts. Soak half: run with {:validate :warn} collecting :mycelium/warnings + :on-trace timing.
- Halt/resume + WorkflowStore + enqueue-resume is simultaneously durable mid-loop resume, the human gate, and the arbiter steer - one mechanism, continuous trace across halts. Resume token = the FSM current-state-id KEYWORD, a pointer into the graph not a snapshot: sessions MUST pin their manifest version or a hot-swap strands them on a renamed state.
- Errors: provider failures via :resilience on :llm/infer + dispatch on :mycelium/resilience-error; tool failures stay errors-as-data (run-tool result maps already are); unexpected throws via :error-groups; wall-clock via graph :timeouts. Stateful resilience lives in the compiled object - a hot-swap resets every circuit breaker.
- Constraints are the mutation protocol's teeth: {:must-follow :tool/dispatch :then :journal/record} makes 'nothing model-visible goes unjournaled' a compile-time invariant an agent edit cannot remove silently.
- Fragments = per-project loop overrides (.samizdat re-wires exits; host interceptors apply). Subworkflows (register-workflow-cell!) = the delegation primitive (child loop as one cell, contract schema, :success/:failure dispatches; parent interceptors do NOT reach children).
- llm-guide.md ships verbatim as the manifest-authoring prompt; cell-brief for delegation, reassignment-brief for repair loops.
GOTCHAS (verified in source): (1) manifest->workflow forwards only :joins :input-schema :interceptors :resilience :transforms - :timeouts/:error-groups/:constraints must be merged in by our loader or they silently vanish. (2) manifest->workflow mutates the global cell registry (.addMethod + set-cell-meta!) - serialize activation; soak in a fresh registry or process. (3) The schema-chain validator and enumerate-paths prune on visited, so a cyclic loop is checked for iteration 1 only and nothing bounds iterations - own turn counter + :default edge to halt. (4) EDN dispatch preds eval as host code in this port - agent-authored manifests are arbitrary code execution; validate/soak/rollback is the guard.
acceptance_criteria: Harness solves a trivial Clojure task end to end in a live run against DeepSeek; kill -9 mid-run then resume completes it; the loop definition is inspectable and editable from the REPL.

title: tasks table (dirge schema, renamed) + model-facing task tools
description: Copy dirge's issues schema (~/src/dirge-code/dirge/src/extras/issue_db.rs:240) as a table named tasks: id, title, body, status (open|in_progress|blocked|done|cancelled with alias normalization), priority, created/updated/closed_at. Generalize epic_id -> parent_id plus a type column (epic is a type of task; hierarchy depth is the model's choice). Keep the active-vs-backlog split (session_id NULL = backlog), board ordering (status -> priority -> updated_at), and origin-lineage session normalization so the board survives compaction/resume. Add contract fields (spec text + test file refs) for delegation. Model-facing tools: create/list/show/update/claim/close.
acceptance_criteria: Live run where the model works the board through tools; migrations tested; board state survives kill and resume.

title: Prune veriframe to the general core, rename namespaces to samizdat
description: Remove engine/{lean_repl,lean_pool,lean_search,smt,smt_templates,octave,prolog}, agent/{faithful,verdict,consensus}, bench/, tools/lean-*, and the formal-methods bulk of agent/tools.clj. Un-leak lean assumptions from state.clj, loop.clj, beam.clj (verification-tools, the :explore/:build phase machine, engine requires). Keep store/*, llm/* incl fence, agent/{arbiter,gates,claims,critic,resume,beam,state,loop}, events, system, config, engine/proc, api/*, server. Rename veriframe.* -> karamazov.* (only maestro.clj carries the new ns today).
acceptance_criteria: Repo compiles on jolt, remaining tests green, server boots, resume-by-replay still works on a pruned run.

title: Port mycelium executor layer onto jolt maestro
description: Vendor mycelium namespaces from ~/src/mycelium-clj/mycelium: cell, schema, validation, workflow, manifest, fragment, compose, store, queue, dev, orchestrate, core. workflow.clj is pure Clojure and should run unchanged - only its maestro dependency changes (see maestro port task). Skip resilience.clj (resilience4j is JVM-bound; veriframe llm/client.clj already owns retry). malli comes in as a dep - it is in jolt's library conformance manifest. Note: the cell registry is the plugin loader; plugins must fit into the mycelium graph because they are part of the state machine.
acceptance_criteria: mycelium test suite green under jolt, including compile-time checks (reachability, dispatch coverage, schema-chain walk) and halt/resume tokens.

title: Port maestro to jolt (drop sci and promesa)
description: src/karamazov/maestro.clj:5 TODO already says it: replace sci with native eval for EDN dispatch predicates (jolt has real runtime eval; safety comes from soak+rollback, not interpretation sandboxing) and replace promesa with core.async or fibers for the async path (keep run-sync as the default driver). Port maestro's test suite from the upstream repo.
acceptance_criteria: maestro tests green under jolt; a data-defined FSM with EDN predicates compiles, runs sync and async, and resumes from a serialized {:trace :data :current-state-id} map.

title: Samizdat harness v0
description:
Self-hosting agentic harness for Clojure/jolt development, DeepSeek-first. Three rings: kernel (journal, event bus, store, secrets, executor lifecycle - agent-immutable), executor (mycelium/maestro workflow layer; the agentic loop is an EDN manifest in the db, hot-swappable via checkpoint -> validate -> soak -> commit/rollback), capabilities (nREPL, clojure-lsp, shell as plugins). Every plugin is a cell in the mycelium graph - part of the state machine - and declares pure vs effectful.

Working agreement: one feature at a time; small chunks, each wired in and proven end to end in a live run before moving on; nothing merges unwired or half-baked. Store starts on sqlite behind mycelium store/queue protocols and swaps to dolt via doltera (jolt MySQL wire client, in progress at ~/src/jolt-lang/doltera). Security: env vars and secrets live only in the shell interaction layer - the model references them symbolically, never sees values. Prolog engine deferred until v0 runs live.

title: Migrate the beam onto the loop manifest
description: Interim state after the loop-as-manifest milestone: the single-branch driver runs the manifest-compiled workflow while beam.clj keeps its own run-turn composition - one source of cell behavior, two drivers. This task removes the second driver: the beam schedules branches as workflow executions (per-turn stepping via halt boundaries or per-turn compiled runs), so the manifest is the ONLY definition of the loop and agent edits to it govern beam runs too. Natural companion to the multi-agent work: subworkflow-as-cell becomes the delegation primitive there.
acceptance_criteria: beam.clj no longer composes turn logic outside the manifest; full suite green; a manifest edit changes beam-run behavior in a live run.

title: Swap store to dolt via doltera
description: Implement the mycelium store/queue protocols and the veriframe store layer over doltera (~/src/jolt-lang/doltera - jolt MySQL wire-protocol client, in progress). Behavior snapshots become dolt commits, mutation rollback becomes dolt revert, and the db is shareable in git repos. Blocked on doltera readiness - do not start until it is usable.
design: doltera v0.2.0 is tagged and usable: https://github.com/jolt-lang/doltera (MySQL wire-protocol client in jolt; src/doltera/wire.clj, hash.clj). No longer blocked on upstream readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Full suite green on dolt; live run including a manifest edit rolled back via dolt revert; db clones via git.

title: Recursive decomposition with contracts, collaborative implement/review
description: Agent decides split depth recursively; each delegation carries a contract + tests as the spec (mycelium orchestrate briefs are nearly this verbatim). Subagents run as fibers sharing the store; the claims registry prevents duplicated work; an implementer never reviews its own work - separate review gate, the veriframe/dirge pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Live run: a non-trivial feature lands via at least two collaborating agents, with review, tracked on the board.
notes:
Hivemind additions: competing solutions arbitrate as append-only sibling rows (version-bump pattern), not merge conflicts; the pure write-gate (bounded diff budget, protected sections) from the .14 design is the zero-cost first review layer before any LLM review runs. Hivemind has no decomposition/handoff protocol to copy - ours comes from mycelium orchestrate briefs as planned.
Physics-of-Agents findings (research/2608.16578v1): reviewer independence must be structural, not prompted - an adversarial-instructed reviewer sharing the implementer's message stream still converges (discordant couplings are weak, concordant dominate). The review agent gets a fresh context containing only the artifact + contract + tests, never the implementer's reasoning or messages. Never decide by counting agent votes: below the critical temperature the dynamics produce agreement regardless of merit, so vote-counting measures the temperature, not the truth - only externally verified evidence (tests, compiler, REPL results) decides, which re-states veriframe's judge-not-vote consensus rule with a mechanistic basis. Competing solutions must stay isolated until an EXTERNAL evaluator picks: persistent splits are unstable (weak repulsion), so competitors allowed to talk pre-evaluation will merge/converge rather than stay genuinely distinct.

title: Shared feature workspace + agent messaging
description: One feature at a time; agents split parts of it. Shared context: feature-scoped artifacts/failures pool (veriframe's, kept) plus durable mailbox messaging over the events bus. Private context: per-agent working state stays out of peers' windows. Context assembly composes shared breadcrumbs + private detail under an explicit token budget so nothing overflows.
design:
Hivemind findings (paths under /Users/yogthos/src/hivemind/src). Headline: hivemind has NO agent-to-agent messaging - no mailboxes, pub/sub, request/reply, roles, voting, or handoff protocol anywhere in ~57k LOC. Its collaboration is purely stigmergic: agents leave traces in a shared DB, later agents read them. So our mailbox/messaging layer comes from our own events bus as planned; what hivemind contributes is the shared-workspace discipline:
- Lease-with-TTL, not locks (docs/meta.ts:9-20,47,138): claim a turn by stamping {claimed_by, claimed_at}; a claim older than the TTL is dead and stealable, so a crashed agent needs no cleanup. Verify claims by READ-BACK, not by update row counts. Keep the commit point separate from the work: the done-watermark advances only at an explicit commit, so a half-done cycle is idempotently redone and a worker that lost its lease is refused at commit ({committed:false, reason:lost-lease}). Maps directly onto our claims registry + journal.
- Append-only + version-bump rows, read = latest-per-key (deeplake-schema.ts:180-189): every shared artifact (task state, review verdicts, competing patches) is an appended v=N+1 row, never a mutated cell. Audit, time-travel, and no lost-update races for free; competing solutions become sibling rows to arbitrate rather than merge conflicts.
- Scope column with fallback resolution (docs/branch-scope.ts, docs/private-store.ts): one column - shared vs agent:<id> vs local - with reads defaulting shared and falling through. That is the whole shared-vs-private context mechanism. Pair with fingerprint-gated promotion (docs/promote.ts): private work graduates to shared only when a content fingerprint proves it still describes what shared currently has - no LLM re-check.
- Pure synchronous write-gate on shared content (docs/gate.ts:14-23,84): bounded changed-lines budget (their 40-line 'textual learning rate'), no dangling references, protected sections a cheap agent may never rewrite. Catches the dominant multi-agent failure - one agent rewriting another's work wholesale - with no model in the path.
- Injection format contract for cross-agent context (hooks/shared/recall-format.ts:136-183): mandatory attribution (who/when/where, no author -> no injection), hard char cap, verbatim-fact sections over prose gists, untrusted text rendered inert with explicit data-not-instructions framing. Cross-agent prompt injection is MORE dangerous for us than for hivemind since our agents are concurrent and co-manipulating - treat every peer-authored block this way.
- Always-on telemetry for every injection decision (recall.ts:9-11,239): {injected|below|none|timeout|error, score, source} to a sink; shared-context relevance cannot be tuned without it.
acceptance_criteria: Two agents on one feature exchange messages and share findings; neither context overflows; message history is durable and replayable.
notes:
Physics-of-Agents findings (research/2608.16578v1, Stanford; Ising-model fit over 10k LLM-agent communities, 75-97% predictive accuracy incl. unseen graph families):
- Communities operate BELOW the critical social temperature: agents start indifferent, build conviction monotonically, and lock in. Agreement among agents that have been reading each other is substantially a thermodynamic artifact of message exchange, not evidence.
- Concordant couplings dominate discordant ones in every model tested (effective friendly pull 0.99-3.03 vs unfriendly push <=0.73, sometimes negative) - even agents INSTRUCTED to be adversarial get dragged toward agreement. Prompting cannot hold a dissenting position; only structural isolation (no channel at all, J=0) can.
- Truth-seeking pull (correct neighbors pull harder) exists only where positions are objectively checkable; on subjective questions the same dynamics amplify the models' shared bias.
Design consequences for this task: the communication topology IS a design variable with predictable consequences - make who-hears-whom-when explicit config, journaled per message, so the effective graph is observable and experimentable. Default topology: independent-first (branches work with no peer channel), then share VERIFIED ARTIFACTS rather than opinions/messages - an artifact carries grounding, a message carries social pressure. Full shared context for everyone = fully-connected friendly graph = maximal herding. Order of information matters because initial conditions pick the basin: a fresh agent gets spec+tests BEFORE any sibling conclusions.
The LEVERAGE framing - the paper is a control theory, and the harness owns all three knobs: topology J (who hears whom, when), initial priming g_i (what enters an agent's context first), and grounding kappa (whether shared positions are externally verified). Effective collaboration = scheduling them per phase of work, expressed as workflow-manifest data:
1. DIVERGE (approach generation): J = identity. No peer channels, deliberately varied priming per branch (different techniques/constraints in the opening context) - diversity is manufactured before contact because it cannot survive contact.
2. GROUND (work): only verified artifacts cross, labeled with their evidence. The truth-seeking pull (correct neighbors pull harder) is the one pro-collaboration force worth amplifying, and it only operates on checkable positions - so the shared field is built exclusively from checked positions.
3. EVALUATE: external verdict (tests/benchmark/human), never inter-agent debate or vote.
4. CONVERGE (after the decision): open channels wide and broadcast the winner. Below-critical-temperature lock-in is a FEATURE here - the same herding that is dangerous pre-decision is fast, durable coordination post-decision; conviction buildup makes the alignment stick.
Also: the contract+tests spec is the strongest alignment instrument we have - it sets every agent's intrinsic field identically on the WHAT while isolation preserves diversity on the HOW. Subjective calls (architecture, naming, scope) never go to the collective - herding amplifies shared model bias where no kappa exists; route to explicit criteria, a single decider, or the human gate.

title: Context management: compaction and lineage
description: Dirge-informed: usage-threshold ladder triggers a fold at the turn boundary; a fold produces a durable checkpoint (intent/summary) plus pruned context; origin lineage keeps conversation identity across folds; circuit breaker degrades to prune-only after summarizer failures. Design notes to follow from the dirge survey.
design:
Dirge basis (paths under /Users/yogthos/src/dirge-code/dirge/src):
- Ladder (agent/agent_loop/context_manager.rs:12-42), ratios over effective window = min(model_window, 250k target): 0.60 tighten per-tool-result cap 3000->1000 tok; 0.75 normal fold (20% tail); 0.78 aggressive fold (10% tail); 0.80 exit-with-summary ends the turn; 0.90 pre-first-call fold. A cheap pre-send snip that frees >=10% suppresses a normal fold (compression.rs:175-180).
- Prune and summarize are distinct passes: prune (compression.rs:606) never calls a model - oversized tool results outside the protected head(2)/tail(5) become shape-preserving one-line synopses. Summarize is the LLM pass: 14-section schema (compression.rs:926-975) where '## Active Task' is 'the single most important field' and must capture EMERGENT follow-up work, not the original assignment; budget = 20% of compressed tokens, floor 2k, ceiling 12k; folded material is fenced as untrusted with a delimiter-collision pre-check that aborts the fold; the spliced summary preamble says reference-not-instructions and names session_search for recovery.
- Circuit breaker: 3 consecutive summarizer failures latches prune-only (still emits a distinct event so the failure signal survives); 120s summarizer timeout counts as failure. No-progress guard (run.rs:1898-1920): a fold that changed nothing must not rotate the session or re-trigger - unfoldable overhead (system prompt + tool schemas) above threshold otherwise causes an infinite re-fold loop, observed in the wild.
- Incremental background checkpoints: threshold schedule fires non-destructive off-loop summaries; the next real fold reuses one via a generation guard instead of an inline LLM call (run.rs:1673-1700).
- Goal survival: session_checkpoints table where intent is WRITE-ONCE (the upsert deliberately never updates intent, only summary+revision - session_db.rs:920-943); resume prepends 'Original request: {intent}'; the task board is durable state re-injected from the db each run (bounded reminder), so compaction cannot lose it.
- Copy the eval too: compaction_recall.rs plants canary facts (path, code loc, error string, config value, token, number) in the folded region and asserts they reach the summarizer; run it in CI.
acceptance_criteria: Long live run crosses at least two compactions with the goal intact and board/journal consistent.
notes: Hivemind additions: rolling checkpoint summaries every N messages / T hours with a per-session sidecar counter + lock (docs/SUMMARIES.md); the ## Next Steps section is the handoff primitive, and their session-start rule is worth copying verbatim - reconcile the summary with current git state BEFORE acting on it (hooks/session-start.ts:~68). Bounded local queue with a GC ceiling if agents buffer events (hooks/session-queue.ts:74-77 - added after a 39.9GB unflushable queue incident).

title: Long-term knowledge in db + breadcrumb context
description: Durable knowledge store informed by dirge's memories table (kind/tier/confidence/salience/superseded_by - design notes to follow from the dirge survey). Context assembly injects a compact breadcrumb index (ids + one-liners), never full content; model-facing retrieval tools (FTS over journal/artifacts/failures, fetch-by-id) let agents follow up. Tool descriptions must teach the breadcrumb pattern so agents know the information exists and how to reach it.
design:
Dirge basis (paths under /Users/yogthos/src/dirge-code/dirge/src):
- memories model (extras/memory_db.rs): kinds semantic/episodic/procedural/working/identity/overview (:52-70); two tiers - 'hot' renders verbatim into the system prompt, 'breadcrumb' renders as a one-line index (uid + kind + first-line preview) the model dereferences on demand. Budgets are chars with a reserved toehold for working memories (:168-186). Eviction is DEMOTION to breadcrumb, not deletion (:915-925); only breadcrumb overflow tombstones. Salience = per-kind base + use reinforcement / disuse decay (extras/salience.rs) + effectiveness bonus for procedural only.
- The index block's literal preamble teaches the pattern: 'Overflow memories... still active, just not inlined. Fetch full text with memory(action=expand...); search everything with memory(action=search...)' - format_for_system_prompt at extras/memory_db.rs:665-727, self-described as the matryoshka stub-and-expand pattern.
- supersede writes a NEW corrected entry and retires the old as an audit record (superseded_by) - never rewrite in place; graduation (extras/memory_graduation.rs) boosts recurring near-duplicates (Jaccard >= 0.80 clustering) without merging, idempotent via graduation_ledger.
- Retrieval surface: session_search tool (agent/tools/session_search.rs:83) - FTS5 over past sessions with DISCOVERY/SCROLL/BROWSE modes, advertised to the model as zero LLM cost; memory expand/search (agent/tools/memory.rs:131-148); automatic pre-recall injects matches headed 'hints, not instructions' and dedups against live context (agent/agent_loop/run.rs:2132-2165).
- Load-bearing contract: the compaction summary preamble NAMES session_search as the recovery path for folded detail. Copy that: every summarization/demotion must leave a breadcrumb naming the tool that recovers the full content.
Karamazov mapping: memories table + tier column in the store; breadcrumb index assembled by the context-assembly cell; retrieval tools over journal/artifacts/failures FTS (veriframe already has the FTS tables).
acceptance_criteria: e2e: knowledge written in run A is recalled in run B via breadcrumb -> fetch, without full-content injection; context size stays bounded.
notes: Hivemind additions (paths under /Users/yogthos/src/hivemind/src): gate-before-retrieve - a cheap regex classifier decides whether a prompt is recall-worthy before any search runs (hooks/shared/recall-gate.ts:90), precision-biased, one hit only, hard char cap; whole path deadline-bounded with real cancellation and fail-to-silence (hooks/recall.ts:63,215). Summaries are structured markdown (## Key Facts / ## Decisions / ## Next Steps) and recall excerpts the verbatim-fact sections, not the prose gist (recall-format.ts:64,82). Their semantic-only search is a workaround for an unindexed backend - keep our lexical/FTS + structured filters (task-id, file, agent-id) as primary. Log every injection decision to a telemetry sink from day one.

title: Self-modification: checkpoint -> validate -> soak -> commit/rollback
description: Kernel-owned mutation protocol for the loop manifest and cells: snapshot (db checkpoint; dolt commit once doltera lands), recompile with mycelium static checks (rejects structurally broken edits before anything runs), soak (shadow-run the next step or a holdout, stubbing effectful cells via the purity marks), then commit or auto-rollback with the failed mutation journaled as a negative constraint. Model-facing tools to view and edit the running workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Live run: agent edits its own loop manifest successfully; a deliberately broken edit is rejected or rolled back without downtime; the failure lands in the journal.

title: clojure-lsp capability seam
description: stdio JSON-RPC provider via jolt process; narrow ops per the dsh lsp exemplar: definition, references, hover, diagnostics - no raw JSON-RPC escape hatch. Model-facing tools registered in the manifest.
acceptance_criteria: Live run: model navigates an unfamiliar codebase via lsp tools and lands a correct edit.

title: nREPL capability seam
description: Promote dev/nrepl_client.clj into a capability seam (dsh pattern: narrow service definition + provider + model-facing tools): eval, load-file, doc, completions, ns inspection over jolt sockets. Tool descriptions must teach REPL-driven flow (eval small, inspect, then edit). Registered as cells/tools in the manifest.
acceptance_criteria: Live run: model develops a function REPL-first against a project nREPL and its tests pass.

title: Mark cells pure vs effectful
description: Extend cell-spec with an effects declaration (:pure true, or :effects [:fs :net :proc ...]). Surface it in workflow->dot, cell-briefs, and validation (warn on undeclared cells). Purpose: reasoning about the state machine, and letting the mutation-protocol soak stub effectful cells.
acceptance_criteria: Purity visible in dev tooling and orchestration briefs; validation flags undeclared cells; tests cover a pure and an effectful cell.

title: Per-project .samizdat config layering
description: dsh-style layers: global defaults -> project .karamazov (manifests, cells, gates, tools) -> runtime patches. Project workflows and tasks ride along in git (dolt db in-repo once doltera lands).
acceptance_criteria: A project overrides a gate threshold and adds a cell without touching global config, verified in a live run.

title: Collective-dynamics observability (behaviors layer, deferred)
description: User-space plugin, after the multi-agent loop runs live. Cheap derived metrics over the journal, from research/2608.16578v1: per-agent stance-flip counts (frozen/switcher/intermittent/oscillator archetypes - an oscillator is wasted spend, a too-early frozen consensus is a herding alarm), and per-feature net-opinion/conviction analogues over collaborating agents. The paper shows these regimes are predictable from topology + initial states, so the harness journaling who-heard-whom (task .14) is what makes topology experiments measurable. Candidate self-modification target: the agent tuning its own communication graph against these metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Live multi-agent run produces archetype/conviction metrics from the journal alone; a deliberately over-connected topology triggers the herding alarm.

title: Embedded prolog engine (deferred)
description: Deferred until v0 runs live. An embedded prolog (FFI or native Scheme on Chez), not a call-out to an external binary, offered as a general model-facing tool: prove facts on demand and query the harness's own state-machine graph.
acceptance_criteria: Live run: model states facts/rules and runs a query against its own workflow graph via the tool.
